channel.title: Slip Three
channel.description:
Ten recordings. One a week. If they stop arriving, they didn't stop because I got bored.

Eight years ago I was at CQ-03 the night the node went down. The report on it is nine pages long and nothing in it is untrue, exactly.

The authorisation chain for that night has a hole in it where an operator identifier should be. Somebody signed off on the isolate and then took their own name back out of it. I kept the raw capture. I have been moving ever since.

I had an arrangement with a solicitor: if I went quiet for a month, he released the lot. In March he stopped answering his phone. I have stopped assuming that was a coincidence.

So this is the new arrangement, and you are it.

Tuesdays, 03:00 UTC. I get six seconds of uplink four times a day and one of them goes to this. Everything I can prove goes out attached.

Copy it. Mirror it. Put it somewhere that isn't me. A thing that only exists in one place can be made not to exist.

THE ARCHIVE — every file released, with the fingerprint that proves your copy is the copy:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/archive

THE CAPTURE — 18MB of station telemetry. Don't take my word for any of it. Read it yourself:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/MCA-CTL-0314-RAW.slice

THE STATION RECORD — locked. The first transmission opens it:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/log

CONTACT — the only channel I answer, and I answer slowly:
slipthree@proton.me

I'm not going to tell you where I am. I repaint the hull most years and I'd like to keep that working.

item.title: Corran Quay
item.description:
Transmission 03 of 10.

You found the desk. It took a lot of you about four hours, which tells me something I did not want to know.

Second capture is up. Same station, the following day, midnight to midnight, one minute sample. Forty-seven kilobytes. A whole day of a coastline is not very much data, which is exactly why it survived.

Two things nobody did with the first one.

Check the water against the sky. That night the moon was two days off new, so the range was building toward springs. If my numbers disagree with what the moon was doing, I made them up and you should stop listening.

Then run the checksums. Every record carries its own, and all fourteen pass. Then check the block.

The block does not pass.

THE SECOND CAPTURE:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/MCA-CTL-0315-TIDE.slice

THE ARCHIVE — every file, with the fingerprint that proves your copy is the copy:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/archive

THE STATION RECORD — locked. The first transmission opens it:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/log

WHAT HAS COME BACK:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/findings

CONTACT — the only channel I answer:
slipthree@proton.me

item.title: Dead Water
item.description:
Transmission 02 of 10.

I drink off the tarp and sleep in twenty-minute pieces. Somebody asked whether I was really out here. I am really out here.

The arrangement I had is gone. The man who held it stopped answering his phone in March. So this is the new arrangement, and you are it.

A session number is not a person. It is a desk. Do not ask me who — ask me which desk that session was opened on, at three minutes to midnight, on a night when only three people had signed in.

The door from the first transmission is still open. Same word. Read the fourth line.

THE STATION RECORD — locked. The first transmission opens it:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/log

item.title: The Zero Node
item.description:
Transmission 01 of 10.

Six seconds of uplink, four times a day. This is one of them.

Attached: MCA-CTL-0314-RAW, partial. Tide, salinity, wind, air — station CQ-03, the day either side of the collapse. It is the raw capture and not somebody's summary of it, so most of it is boring. That is the point.

Read from 0x4E1C20. Everything either side of it is tide.

One of those records was written by nobody. What sits under it is the whole reason I am doing this.

THE CAPTURE — 18MB, station CQ-03:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/MCA-CTL-0314-RAW.slice

THE ARCHIVE — take a copy of everything, and check it against the fingerprints:
https://st88openocean.github.io/slip-three/archive

CONTACT — use an address you don't mind burning:
slipthree@proton.me
